reasoning.overall: Mexico hosts the opening match of the 2026 World Cup at the Estadio Azteca. The massive home crowd and extreme altitude (2,200m) provide a significant advantage. South Africa has a solid defensive structure and counter-attacking threat through Percy Tau, but Mexico's superior squad quality, led by Santiago Giménez and Edson Álvarez, combined with the environmental factors, makes a home win highly probable.
reasoning.t1_result: Mexico is heavily favored due to home advantage and altitude. A 2-0 win is most likely, with South Africa struggling to maintain intensity in the second half.
reasoning.t2_player: Giménez leads the line for Mexico, supported by Lozano and Antuna. South Africa relies on Williams in goal and Tau for transitions.
reasoning.t3_events: Mexico will press early to get an early goal. South Africa might pick up yellow cards trying to disrupt the rhythm. Substitutions around the 60th minute will be crucial for South Africa due to altitude fatigue.
reasoning.t4_stats: Mexico will dominate possession (around 62%) and shot count, while South Africa will have more defensive actions and rely on quick counters.
